terroir.title: Quinta da Touriga-Chã
terroir.subtitle: Schist, sun, and the Douro Superior.

soil.title: The Schistous Soil
soil.text: Pre-Cambrian schist — fractured, vertical plates of metamorphic rock that force vine roots deep into the earth. This ancient geology provides extraordinary drainage, forcing the vines to struggle and concentrate flavour. The schist absorbs heat during the scorching summer days and radiates it gently through the night, extending the ripening period and building aromatic complexity.

climate.title: The Climate
climate.text: The Douro Superior enjoys over 3,000 hours of sunlight annually — among the highest in Europe. Diurnal temperature shifts of up to 20°C preserve natural acidity while allowing full phenolic ripeness. The Marão and Montemuro mountain ranges shelter the valley from Atlantic influence, creating a continental microclimate of extremes that forges wines of power and finesse.

expression.title: The Expression
expression.text: Schist and sun — the two forces that define our wines. The fractured rock imparts a distinctive mineral signature: graphite, wet stone, and smoke. The relentless Douro sun builds concentration and depth. Together, they produce wines of remarkable structure, aromatic intensity, and a singular sense of place that cannot be replicated anywhere else in the world.

viticulture.title: Viticulture
viticulture.subtitle: Safeguarding the genetic heritage of the Douro through integrated, sustainable production. Every vine planted with intention. Every root system a direct connection to the fractured schist below.
viticulture.text: The vineyard is planted predominantly to Touriga Nacional — the variety José António was the first to champion as Portugal's finest. Low yields, high density, and a philosophy of minimum intervention allow the personality of each parcel to speak without interference. The result is fruit of extraordinary concentration and aromatic precision.

vinificacao.title: Winemaking
vinificacao.subtitle: The transformation from grape to wine is an act of custodianship, not creation. The fruit arrives at the winery and is treated with the reverence it commands.
vinificacao.text: Fermentation in small lagares and temperature-controlled stainless steel. Ageing in French oak barrels, used with subtlety to refine tannins without masking the fruit. The goal is transparency — a wine that tastes of its vineyard, its vintage, and nothing else.

adega.title: The Winery
adega.subtitle: Built in 2004, the adega is an architectural statement of intent. Designed with intentional false symmetries, it blends raw functionality with award-winning aesthetic integration into the Douro valley.
adega.text: Concrete, schist, and light. The building follows the contour of the land, sinking into the hillside to maintain a constant temperature. Gravity-flow design minimises pumping. Every decision — from the orientation of the fermentation hall to the depth of the barrel cellar — serves the wine.

familia.title: The Family
familia.subtitle: Six generations. One valley. An unbroken thread of dedication to the Douro.
familia.text: José António Castro Ramos Pinto Rosas (1919–1996) — founder of ADVID, co-creator of modern vineyard systems, and revered internationally as the Pioneer of the Douro. At 72, he found a virgin 20-hectare property near Vila Nova de Foz Côa and planted 8.5 hectares from scratch, with over 80% Touriga Nacional. Today, his son Jorge Rosas, the fifth generation, continues that legacy from the award-winning 2004 winery.

jarpr.name: José António Rosas
jarpr.text: Founder of ADVID. Co-creator of modern Douro vineyard systems. Portugal's representative at L'Office International du Vin. Founder of the Confraria do Vinho do Porto. Known internationally as the Pioneer of the Douro. At 72, he planted 8.5 hectares from scratch — his final and greatest project.

bio.title: José António Ramos Pinto Rosas
paragraphs: Dedicated his entire professional career to the Port Wine Industry and to the oldest appellation in the world – the Douro Valley. Different international wine writers have referred to José Antonio as the “Douro Pope” (in Le Porto, by Chantale Lecouty, page 145), or “The Prophet of the Douro”, or “the Pioneer do Douro”, thanks to his great contribution to the development of this Region.

José António Rosas, undertook the important work that lead to the modern development of this wine district. Always working with the final objective of finding the best solutions to increase both the quality of the wines and the production systems in the Douro Valley.

His creation of the new plantation method “patamares” permitted more mechanization in the vineyards, but together with his nephew João Nicolau de Almeida, “vertical vineyards” where also implemented in the Douro Valley, not only for more mechanization but also for greater plant density, resulting in higher yields per hectare but lower production per vine and higher quality of fruit. They also undertook research into the area’s grape varietals and root stock selections, the results of which have largely been adopted by the majority of the Douro vine growers.

José António was also Portugal’s representative at “L’Office International du Vin”, was founder of the Confraria do Vinho do Porto (Port Wine Brotherhood) & Presidente do Conselho da Administração (CEO) of the Port and Douro wine producer A. Ramos Pinto, Vinhos S.A..

With his strong determination to increase the quality of the wines produced in this Valley, in 1982 he founded the well respected ADVID (Association for the Development of the Douro Valley viticulture), of which he was president until 1996.
José António Rosas was the co-author of the book “The Port Wine” published by the IVDP (Port Wine Institute).

jorge.name: Jorge Rosas
jorge.text: Son of José António. Steward of the Quinta da Touriga-Chã since his father's passing. Built the award-winning 2004 winery. Continues the legacy with the same uncompromising dedication to the Douro, its vineyards, and its wines.
